After passing through the capillaries and venules, blood continues into the veins on the way back to the heart. Veins 
have thinner walls than arteries, because pressures are lower in this portion of the cardiovascular system. Veins also 
dilate in response to fluid. Some veins, like the large veins in the legs, have valves in them to prevent backflow of 
blood (Gupta & Shea, 2022). Once blood has traveled through the veins, it ends up in the heart to start the cycle all 
over again. 
Assessment 
The nurse should complete a client’s assessment by recording manual blood pressure and apical pulse (a pulse 
point on the chest at the apex of the heart). In addition, the nurse should look for other signs and symptoms of 
adequate perfusion, including: 
• Quality and rate of peripheral pulses (carotid auscultation and palpation, brachial, radial, ulnar, femoral, 
popliteal, and pedal) 
• Skin color
